issues.description: The problem statement says the DDNode.successors is a tuple of DDs, but both the template and solution implementations declare successors as a list[DD]. This discrepancy between the textual specification and the code may confuse students about the expected data structure and how to interact with DDNode.successors.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification with the code: update the problem statement to state that DDNode.successors is a list[DD] (or change the code to use tuples consistently). Clearly document the mutability expectations (list vs tuple) so students know whether they may modify successor containers.

issues.description: The problem statement describes DDNode.successors as a "tuple of DDs", whereas both the template and solution implementations declare the attribute as successors: list[DD]. This mismatch between the documented type/name and the actual code may confuse students about the expected data structure when they are instructed not to manipulate DD/DDNode internals.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the wording in problem_statement.md consistent with the code: change the phrase to refer to 'successors is a list of DDs (successors: list[DD])' or otherwise use neutral wording such as 'a sequence of DDs'. Alternatively, update the code annotations to use tuple[DD] if tuples are intended, but ensure all artifacts use the same representation.
